issue_context.title: LE Audio: Add BAP unicast client long write support
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently the BAP unicast client can only send control point writes with the size of the MTU. Since some values such as the metadata (used in the update metadata and enable operations) may be up to 255 octets, we should be able to support that. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add support for sending control point operations of 255 (metadata) + 1 (ase ID). This will require us to extend the `ep_buf` or reuse the `read_buf` that is already implemented by https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/54363.

Keep in mind that the upper layer may want to send the enable/update metadate request to multiple ASEs, and that we may need to either restrict it to a single write, or add multiple buffers to support concurrent writes. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
This will also allows us to better support sending the control point operations with multiple ASEs at once, if we add support for that in the API.

review_comments: Please avoid including internal headers. You could move the `BT_ATT_BUF_SIZE` to public `include/zephyr/bluetooth/att.h` instead.

I agree, but this will require significant changes to ATT. I'll rather do that in a separate PR. If that PR merges before this, I'll update this PR; vice versa if this merges first I'll modify this in that PR.

Don't you forgot to check whether `client->busy` is false?

If I understand correctly, if the CP operation does not fit the MTU, the `bt_gatt_write` will be used, otherwise `bt_gatt_write_without_response`. Is it because, the stack will fallback to `Write Long Characteristic Value` in such case? If so, it would be nice if you could add a comment here.
It gave compiler warnings for me otherwise. It should be included in any case, since the file uses `BT_L2CAP_SDU_RX_MTU`, `BT_L2CAP_SDU_TX_MTU` and `BT_L2CAP_RX_MTU` which are defined by `l2cap.h`.
